dek: A 147-country study says connection beats money and success every time.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Oxford researchers studied people across *147 countries* and found 3 simple questions predict happiness better than money.

slides.label: The 3 Questions
slides.text: Do you eat meals with others? Do you expect strangers to be trustworthy? Do you regularly help other people?

slides.label: Meal Sharing
slides.text: Happiness peaked at *13 meals* a week shared with others, far more than most Americans manage. Any amount still helps.

slides.label: Trusting Strangers
slides.text: People who believed a lost wallet would be returned to them were measurably *happier*, even though most underestimate the odds.

slides.label: Built On Trust
slides.text: Amazon, Uber, Etsy and eBay all run on strangers trusting strangers, proof the instinct pays off more than we think.

slides.label: Being Kind
slides.text: Donating, volunteering and helping strangers boost happiness most when it's a *free choice* with a clear, visible impact.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: For underrepresented founders and workers told to grind solo, this says *community and trust* build real happiness too.

caption_instagram:
Oxford's 2025 World Happiness Report just confirmed what community already knows: connection beats cash when it comes to joy. Researchers studied people across 147 countries and found that eating meals together, trusting strangers, and helping others predict happiness more than money or career success ever could.

The data is wild: happiness peaked at 13 shared meals a week, and people who believed a lost wallet would be returned to them were measurably happier, even though most of us underestimate how kind strangers really are. Even companies like Amazon, Uber, and Etsy are built on that same leap of trust.

For our community, this hits different. We're often told to grind solo and hustle harder, but the science says showing up for each other, breaking bread, lending a hand, trusting your people, is the real wealth builder.

How many meals do you share with others weekly? Give a number.

caption_linkedin:
Oxford University's 2025 World Happiness Report studied 147 countries and found a surprising formula for happiness: connection, not capital.

The three strongest predictors were sharing meals with others, expecting strangers to be trustworthy, and regularly helping people through donations, volunteering, or small acts of kindness. Happiness peaked at 13 shared meals a week. People who believed a lost wallet would be returned to them scored higher on happiness too.

For founders and operators, this is more than a feel good stat. Trust is the business model behind Amazon, Uber, Etsy, and eBay, all built on strangers trusting strangers. Kindness also pays off best when it's chosen freely and the impact is visible, not forced by pressure from a boss or client.

If you're building a team or a company, the research suggests investing in real connection, shared meals, visible trust, genuine generosity, may do more for retention and morale than another bonus structure.
